authentication: OpenCode Go subscription API key from the Console; Bearer token to https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1/chat/completions; stable x-opencode-session header for routing/caching.
official_permission: Official OpenCode Go documentation exposes Go models to OpenCode and other coding agents, subject to abuse monitoring and privacy-region settings.
capabilities: tool calling supported by the model family
1M context / 384K max output per third-party catalog; verify from /v1/models
quota_behavior: Per-model monthly dollar allowance, with 5-hour (20%) and weekly (50%) sub-limits; each response reports opencode.allowance. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash has a $100 monthly limit on the Go plan.
no_overage_controls: Owner must disable Extra Usage in the OpenCode Console Go page.
Owner must disable credits/balance fallback; only the Go subscription key may be present.
Guard requires an explicit owner attestation before a request is dispatched.
Post-response billing_source must be go/go-plus and cost must be zero; otherwise halt the run and surface a funding violation.
known_limitations: Extra Usage is an account setting; response metadata cannot undo a charge that already occurred.
DeepSeek models may require Global region selection in workspace privacy settings.
The API key is a bearer credential; the Factory must keep it inside its provider boundary.
Model roster, prices and limits change; re-verify before production.
decision: ALLOWED ONLY behind owner attestation, no Extra Usage/credits, a deterministic fake first, and a separate live-test authorization.

authentication: Local Codex sign-in with ChatGPT (`~/.codex/auth.json` or OS keyring); app-server JSON-RPC over stdio/WebSocket/Unix socket. API-key sign-in is a different billing mode and is refused.
official_permission: OpenAI documents app-server as the supported way to embed Codex in a product, including authentication, history, approvals and streamed events. It is an agent integration, not a completion API.
capabilities: its own tools, sandbox, skills, MCP servers and context
quota_behavior: Uses the signed-in ChatGPT plan's shared Work/Codex usage and workspace limits; /status and the usage dashboard expose remaining capacity.
no_overage_controls: Refuse API-key auth (`forced_login_method = chatgpt` where policy permits).
Do not enable credits or extra usage for the Factory workspace.
Do not expose app-server to untrusted clients; keep it loopback/stdio and behind Factory authorization.
Do not silently switch provider or account when limits are reached; fail closed.
known_limitations: It is a complete coding agent: wrapping it as a `ModelProvider` loses approvals, tool semantics, context and cancellation boundaries.
Factory is not a registered Sign in with ChatGPT client; this route relies on local Codex authentication, not Factory OAuth.
Usage exhaustion and credits behavior are account/workspace settings, not a stable API contract.
App-server API surface evolves; pin the Codex version and generated schema.
decision: ALLOWED ONLY as an external coding-agent integration, after a separate owner authorization and with ChatGPT auth pinned.

authentication: Codex SDK controls the local Codex app-server. It inherits the local ChatGPT sign-in; an API key selects API billing instead.
official_permission: OpenAI documents the TypeScript/Python SDK for programmatic coding tasks and internal tools; the Python SDK explicitly controls app-server over JSON-RPC.
capabilities: external tool messages and structured final response
quota_behavior: Same ChatGPT plan/Codex usage as app-server; the SDK itself does not create an allowance.
no_overage_controls: Use a ChatGPT-authenticated Codex home; never pass an API key.
Run with workspace_write or read_only, not full_access, inside Factory's wider confinement.
known_limitations: SDK adds a Node.js/Python runtime dependency that conflicts with Factory's container-native preference unless packaged in the image.
It is an agent, not a completion adapter.
SDK/Codex version compatibility must be pinned.
decision: ALLOWED ONLY as a specialized coding-agent integration; prefer app-server for a Rust host.

display_name: Sign in with ChatGPT — third-party app OAuth
authentication: OAuth client registered with OpenAI; the user grants the app permission to use their ChatGPT plan.
official_permission: OpenAI requires a registered client ID and lists participating apps. Factory is not registered in this experiment.
capabilities: optionally plan usage for eligible apps
quota_behavior: Counts toward the user's existing plan; app limits are caps, not a new allowance.
no_overage_controls: Do not invent an entitlement endpoint.
Do not use an unregistered OAuth client.
known_limitations: No client ID or owner approval in this experiment.
Sign-in permission and plan-usage permission are separate consents.
decision: BLOCKED: requires OpenAI client registration and a separate product/legal review.

official_permission: No official public completion API with ChatGPT subscription OAuth is documented for third parties. OpenCode's bundled integration is an OpenCode implementation, not a Factory entitlement.
no_overage_controls: Forbidden: do not scrape tokens or reverse-engineer private endpoints.
known_limitations: Would violate the Owner's no-unapproved-auth rule.
